name: claude-code
_comment: VERIFIED end-to-end 2026-07-08 against Claude Code 2.1.204 (Windows) via scripts/verify_harness.py — the woken agent read the briefing and echoed the canary token. Flags re-checked 2026-08-28 against current docs + the local CLI (2.1.250 era); not re-run end-to-end since. -p runs a single non-interactive prompt and exits. Permission posture: -p starts in Manual mode with NO prompt to fall back to, so any tool call needing approval silently fails — --allowedTools "Read" pre-approves file reads tool-wide, which also lets the briefing be read wherever it lands (reads outside the working directory otherwise need an approval a headless run can't grant; that's permission scoping, not the Bash-sandbox feature). Alternatives by taste: --add-dir <briefing dir>, --permission-mode dontAsk with an exact allowlist, or --restricted (v2.1.248+) on shared machines. We still do NOT pass --dangerously-skip-permissions: a wake-triggered invocation should go through your normal permission rules unless you've deliberately configured otherwise. Briefings are written to zugamind/data/briefings/ (not the system temp dir); override with ZUGAMIND_BRIEFING_DIR. Set wake_modules/wake_min_salience before running unattended (see examples/harness-configs/README.md) — without a filter this harness wakes for every gated winner. Ships enabled:false like every config in this folder; flipping it to true is always an explicit act.
command: Read the briefing at {briefing_file} and act on it
